title: Triangle compatibility of the trace class
statement:
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times X$ be an admissible correspondence with
coefficient $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$
([def-trf-correspondence]), with fixed scheme $F$, and let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ which is *$c$-invariant*: $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$
set-theoretically, so that $c_1^{-1}(Z)\subset c_2^{-1}(Z)$ and
$c_2^{-1}(U)\subset c_1^{-1}(U)$. Then $u$ induces coefficient morphisms
$u^U$ on $K'=j_!j^*K$ and $u^Z$ on $K''=Ri_*i^*K$: $u^U=[j]_!(u|_U)$ is
the extension by zero of the restriction of $u$ to the open correspondence
$c|_U$ on $c^{-1}(U\times U)=c_2^{-1}(U)$, and $u^Z=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ is the
pushforward of the restriction of $u$ to the closed correspondence
$c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ (in the Frobenius case
these are the pieces $u^U,u^Z$ of [d-curve-pieces]). The triple
$(u^U,u,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed triangles
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$, and the
Verdier trace classes of [def-trf-trace-class] satisfy

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)
$$

in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$.
This is the additivity of the Verdier trace class along a $c$-invariant
open–closed decomposition. It
is *not* asserted for an arbitrary morphism $(u',u,u'')$ of distinguished
triangles in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: for the identity correspondence of a point
that assertion is the additivity of the categorical trace on arbitrary
endomorphisms of distinguished triangles of perfect complexes, which fails
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (2)).

external.place: This is the additivity of the Verdier trace class along a $c$-invariant open–closed decomposition ([Varshavsky, Prop. 1.5.10](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564), proved in his §5.3 by filtered trace maps; classically SGA 5, Exposé III, 4.13).

proof.text:
Let $T=Rc_{1!}Lc_2^*$ and let $v:TK\to K$ be the exceptional adjoint of $u$ under the constructible adjunction supplied by its admissibility datum [def-trf-admissibility]. Only this specified adjunction is needed; the ordinary adjunctions used below are those of [fix-prop-adjunctions]. Put $K_U=j_!j^*K$, $K_Z=Ri_*i^*K$, and write $a:K_U\to K$, $b:K\to K_Z$ for the localization maps of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. All coefficients below remain in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Put $V=c_2^{-1}(U)$ and let $e:V\hookrightarrow C$ be its open immersion. Invariance says $V\subset c_1^{-1}(U)$, so $c_1e=jh$ for a map $h:V\to U$. The open base-change and composition clauses of [prop-functor-package] give
$$TK_U\simeq Rc_{1!}e_!(c_2|_V)^*j^*K\simeq j_!Rh_!(c_2|_V)^*j^*K.$$
The vanishing $j^*Ri_*=0$ and the open adjunction in [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] and [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] therefore give $\operatorname{Hom}(TK_U,K_Z[m])=0$ for every integer $m$. Apply the Hom exactness statements [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], including their rotations, to the target localization triangle and its image under the exact functor $T$. The adjacent groups are $\operatorname{Hom}(TK_U,K_Z[m])$ with $m=0,-1$ or $0,1$, and vanish, so these exact sequences give bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(TK_U,K_U)\xrightarrow{a\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(TK_U,K),\qquad
\operatorname{Hom}(TK_Z,K_Z)\xrightarrow{-\circ Tb}\operatorname{Hom}(TK,K_Z).$$
Thus there are unique $v_U,v_Z$ with $a v_U=v\,Ta$ and $v_Z\,Tb=bv$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-open-extension-adjoint] with $P=C$, $f=c_1$, $t=c_2$, $V=c_2^{-1}(U)$ and $L=j^*K$. It identifies the exceptional adjoint $p_U$ of $u^U$ with the extension by zero of the adjoint of $u|_U$, and gives $a p_U=v\,Ta$. The first bijection of step 1 therefore gives $p_U=v_U$.

source.place: §1.5.9 and §5.3.3, identification of the open graded morphism

proof.text: Put $D=(C\times_{c_1,X}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $g:D\hookrightarrow C$. Invariance makes the second leg factor through $Z$: affine locally its defining ideal pulls back into every prime ideal on $D$, hence to zero because $D$ is reduced. Write $d_1,d_2:D\to Z$ for the two legs. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-closed-basechange-mate] with $f=c_1,t=c_2$. Its $B_K$ identifies $i^*TK$ with $Rd_{1!}d_2^*i^*K$. Put $L=i^*K$ and $w=i^*v\circ B_K^{-1}$. By the definition of restriction in the source (Varshavsky §1.1.8(i)), $u|_Z$ is the exceptional adjoint of $w$ for the specified adjunction [def-trf-admissibility].

Use [lem-trf-proper-coefficient-adjoint] for the diagram $(i,g):(D,d)\to(C,c)$, where both maps are closed immersions and hence proper. It gives the exceptional adjoint of $u^Z=[i,g]_!(u|_Z)$ as
$$q:TK_Z\xrightarrow{Rc_{1!}\gamma}Rc_{1!}Rg_*d_2^*L\xrightarrow{\Xi}Ri_*Rd_{1!}d_2^*L\xrightarrow{Ri_*w}Ri_*L=K_Z.$$
Here $\gamma$ and $\Xi$ have exactly the types and normalization stated in [lem-trf-reduced-closed-basechange-mate]. This applies without assuming the second-leg square Cartesian.

By [lem-trf-reduced-closed-basechange-mate], the ordinary transpose of $q$ under $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ is $w\circ S(\varepsilon_{i,L})\circ B_{K_Z}$, where $S=Rd_{1!}d_2^*$. Its last naturality equation says that the transpose of $q\,Tb$ is $w B_K=i^*v$. The transpose of $bv$ is also $i^*v$, since the ordinary triangle identity of [fix-prop-adjunctions] gives $\varepsilon_{i,L}\circ i^*b=1_L$. Equality of transposes gives $q\,Tb=bv$, so step 1 gives $q=v_Z$. Thus the exceptional adjoints of $v_U,v_Z$ are exactly $u^U,u^Z$.

Choose a bounded complex $M$ representing $K$. By the exactness and short exact sequence in [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf], $F^0M=M$, $F^1M=j_!j^*M$, $F^2M=0$ is a filtered complex with graded complexes $i_*i^*M$ and $j_!j^*M$. Both graded functors are exact: exactness of $i_*i^*$ also follows because the cokernel functor of the natural monomorphism between the exact functors $j_!j^*$ and the identity is exact, by the short exact sequences and the kernel/cokernel exact sequence. Thus quasi-isomorphisms of $M$ become filtered quasi-isomorphisms. This constructs $\widetilde K$ in [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category], with $\omega\widetilde K=K$, $\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde K=K_Z$ and $\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde K=K_U$; finite-Tor constructibility of these pieces follows from [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Use [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] to form $H=R\operatorname{Hom}^F_X(T\widetilde K,\widetilde K)$. The only potentially nonzero negative grade is
$$\operatorname{gr}^{-1}H=R\operatorname{Hom}_X(TK_U,K_Z),$$
which is zero since all its cohomology groups vanish by step 1. The finite filtration and graded conservativity give $t^{<0}H=0$. The truncation triangle then makes $\omega t^{\ge0}H\to\omega H$ invertible. The filtered Hom comparison therefore lifts $v$ uniquely to $\widetilde v:T\widetilde K\to\widetilde K$. Its graded maps satisfy $a\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde v=v\,Ta$ and $(\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde v)Tb=bv$ by naturality of the filtration maps, so uniqueness in step 1 identifies them with $v_U,v_Z$. The filtered exceptional adjunction yields $\widetilde u:Lc_2^*\widetilde K\to Rc_1^!\widetilde K$ with these graded pieces. The functorial filtered truncation triangle supplies all three squares, including the connecting square, of the asserted morphism of localization triangles.

Apply [lem-trf-filtered-trace-additivity] to the filtered adjoint $\widetilde v:T\widetilde K\to\widetilde K$ constructed in step 6. The filtered comparison of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] identifies our finite-coefficient category and operations with the classical filtered category transported from the étale site used in that lemma; its $u$ and $u_r$ are the exceptional adjoints of the underlying and graded maps, hence are $u$ and the $u^Z,u^U$ of step 6. Only grades zero and one can contribute, and step 6 identified them as $(K_Z,u^Z)$ and $(K_U,u^U)$. Its finite sum is therefore $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)$. Commutativity of addition in the target Hom group gives the order displayed in the statement. The traces here are the Verdier classes of [def-trf-trace-class] on the common fixed scheme, before integration or restriction to a geometric point. For the unit's local-term consequence, suppose additionally that $F$ is proper over $s$, and let $B\subseteq F$ be clopen. By [sk-d-local-term], $\operatorname{LT}_B(u)=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\circ e_B$, with the same idempotent $e_B$ for the three classes. Precomposition with $e_B$ is additive in the derived Hom group; applying the $A$-linear integration of [lem-trf-integration-linear] (with $\beta=F$ and scalar $1$) therefore gives
$$\operatorname{LT}_B(u)=\operatorname{LT}_B(u^U)+\operatorname{LT}_B(u^Z).$$
This conditional scalar consequence is distinct from the class identity, which required no properness hypothesis.

proof.text: The qualification at the end of the statement uses only clause (2) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]. Its current statement places the categorical trace on perfect ordinary module complexes, so the three complexes in the warning are in its stated domain. Over $R=\mathbf Z/4$, the outer complexes $R[-1]$ and $R$ and the middle complex $[R\xrightarrow{2}R]$ are bounded finite-free complexes. The cited endomorphism has zero maps on the ends and middle map $(0,2)$ in degrees $0,1$, hence middle trace $0-2=-2\ne0$ and outer traces zero. Thus even perfect complexes do not give trace additivity for arbitrary commuting triangle squares. This is only the warning for the identity correspondence of a point; steps 1–7 prove the geometric identity using the constructed filtered origin. None of those steps uses categorical filtered additivity or invertibility of the coefficient morphism.

$c|_U$ on $c^{-1}(U\times U)=c_2^{-1}(U)$, and $u^Z=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ is the

$c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ (in the Frobenius case
these are the pieces $u^U,u^Z$ of [d-curve-pieces]). The triple
$(u^U,u,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed triangles
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$, and the
Verdier trace classes of [def-trf-trace-class] satisfy

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)
$$

in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$.
This is the additivity of the Verdier trace class along a $c$-invariant
open–closed decomposition. It
is *not* asserted for an arbitrary morphism $(u',u,u'')$ of distinguished
triangles in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: for the identity correspondence of a point
that assertion is the additivity of the categorical trace on arbitrary
endomorphisms of distinguished triangles of perfect complexes, which fails
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (2)).

proof.text:
*The induced morphisms.* Restriction of $u$ to the open correspondence
$c|_U$ uses only $j^*=j^!$ and the inclusions $c_2^{-1}(U)\subset c_1^{-1}(U)$;
the extension by zero $[j]_!(u|_U):c_2^*j_!j^*K\to c_1^!j_!j^*K$ is the
composite of the open $!$-base change $c_2^*j_!\cong j_!(c_2|_U)^*$, of
$j_!(u|_U)$ and of the canonical map $j_!(c_1|_U)^!\to c_1^!j_!$. The
restriction $u|_Z$ exists because $Z$ is $c$-invariant ($c|_Z$ is the
correspondence induced on $c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $u$ pulls back
along the closed immersion of correspondences), and $[i]_!(u|_Z)$ is its
coefficient pushforward along the proper morphism $[i]$ of correspondences,
as in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] and the proper pushforward
of this chapter. That $(u^U,u,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed
triangles is checked by adjunction exactly as in the Frobenius case treated
in the proof of item (2) of the trace-class additivity proposition of this
block, the third square following from the first two and the vanishing
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[1],Ri_*M)=0$.

*Additivity.* The identity of trace classes is
[Varshavsky, Prop. 1.5.10](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564) in our leg
convention (his $c$-morphisms are $c_1^*\mathcal F\to c_2^!\mathcal F$, so
his $c_2^{-1}(Z)$ is our $c_1^{-1}(Z)$ and his $c$-invariance
$c_1(c_2^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$ is our $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$). His proof
(§5.3, Lemma 5.3.2, after Illusie, SGA 5 III 4.13) lifts the trace map to
the filtered derived category $D^bF_{ctf}(X,A)$: the two-step filtration
$j_!j^*K\subset K$ makes $(K,u)$ a filtered $c$-morphism whose graded
pieces are $(j_!j^*K,u^U)$ and $(Ri_*i^*K,u^Z)$, the trace map is a
morphism of filtered bifunctors, and the trace of a filtered $c$-morphism
is the sum of the traces of its graded pieces. The argument needs the
filtered origin of the triple: it is not a consequence of the three squares
commuting in the derived category.

*What the previous argument got wrong.* An earlier proof of this lemma
restricted the trace classes to the geometric points $\bar y$ of $F$ and
claimed $Li_{\bar y}^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$
in general. This is false: the stalk at $\bar y$ of the trace-class source
$R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*K,c_1^!K)$ is not $R\mathcal Hom_A(K_{\bar y},K_{\bar y})$
(for $K=j_!A$ on $\mathbf A^1$ the source is $Rj_*A$, with nonzero stalk at
$0$ although $K_0=0$), and the equality of the local term with the stalk
trace holds only under a contracting hypothesis
([lem-trf-local-term-locality], item (1)). The reduction to the point
normalization is therefore not available, and the filtered argument above
replaces it.
